Hello,

I purchased a BSB NerdOctaxe (12TH/s) from HeliumDeploy on August 18, 2026,
for a total of $424.48, including shipping.

One of the cooling fans has begun malfunctioning. The miner is only
approximately two months old, and I believe this should qualify as a
manufacturing defect covered under warranty.

Your website states that products are covered by a manufacturer’s warranty
of at least one year.

I would prefer to receive a replacement fan rather than return the entire
miner, provided the fan can be replaced without affecting the warranty.

Could you please advise whether you can supply a replacement fan at no
charge or provide the manufacturer’s contact information and instructions
for filing a warranty claim?

I can provide photographs, video of the malfunction, and my PayPal purchase
receipt if needed.

Thank you for your assistance.

Hello,

Thanks for the clear description, and good news first: a failing cooling fan on a NerdOctaxe is not a board fault and the unit does not need to come back to us. The fan on these sits on a standard 4-pin header on the board, so changing it is a plug-and-play job that does not affect the warranty on the miner itself.

Before anything else, three quick checks that take a few minutes and tell us whether the fan itself is really the problem. First, with the miner unplugged from the wall, unplug the fan connector from its header on the board and push it back in firmly; a connector that has worked loose in transit or with vibration is a common cause. Second, power it back up, open the web UI in your browser, set the fan control to manual and the speed to 100 percent, and watch what the suspect fan does: spins up normally, stutters and stalls, or rattles and grinds. Third, if your unit has two fan headers, move the suspect fan to the other header and see if it behaves the same way. If it misbehaves on both headers, the fan is at fault. If it works fine on the other header, the header is the issue and I need to know that, because the verdict changes.

While you are in the UI, please note the chip and VR temperatures it reports, and tell me the firmware version shown. If you see any VREG, TPS or chip-detection error, say so, as that is a different problem entirely and I would want to look at it straight away.

On your warranty question: you do not need to contact the manufacturer or file anything with them. We handle this directly. I have passed your case to our hardware lead today with my finding that this is a fan, not a board fault, and a colleague is picking it up and will confirm the details with you in this thread. The short video of the fan behaving badly and a clear photo of the serial number label on the unit would help them a lot, so please attach those to your reply. The P. receipt is useful too if you do not have the order number to hand.

If you would like faster hands-on help in the meantime, our community Discord is very active and you can reach our hardware lead there: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

Happy to keep digging into this with you once you have run those checks.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

I haven't heard from anyone about my miner and I'm feeling sad, being I
spent the money on this miner and it's sitting here, not running because of
a fan that shouldn't have failed this soon.

Hello Bill,

I am sorry you have been sitting and waiting, and I understand the frustration of having a miner you paid for standing idle over one fan. Your case is with our hardware lead and a colleague is picking it up today to confirm the fan details with you directly in this thread.

In the meantime I do not want the miner sitting there doing nothing, because there is a safe way to keep it running on the good fan while this is sorted. Open the web UI, set fan control to manual and the working fan to 100 percent, and make sure the automatic temperature shutdown is left enabled so the unit protects itself. Then drop the power: lower the ASIC frequency and core voltage a step or two from the stock preset, give it ten or fifteen minutes, and watch the chip and VR temperatures in the UI. If the chip temperature settles below about 60 to 65 degrees C and stays there, it is fine to keep mining at that reduced setting until the new fan is in. If it keeps climbing past that, step the frequency down again, and if it still climbs, shut it down and leave it off. Having the case open and the unit in free air, away from carpet or a closed shelf, helps a lot too.

One more thing worth ruling out while you wait, if you have not already: with the miner unplugged at the wall, unseat the bad fan's connector from its header on the board and push it back in firmly, then power up and watch it at 100 percent. A connector that has worked loose looks exactly like a dead fan. If your board has a second header, moving the suspect fan to it tells us whether the fan or the header is the problem, and that is useful information for the team either way.

When you reply, a short video of the fan misbehaving and a clear photo of the serial number label on the unit will let my colleague move straight ahead without going back and forth with you.

If you want faster hands-on help at any hour, our community Discord is very active and our hardware lead is on it: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

Thanks for your patience, Bill, and tell me the temperatures you see and I will tune it further with you.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
